questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] What type of rock is generally formed by solid-state changes in pre-existing rocks?
A. Igneous
B. Sedimentary
C. Metamorphic
Answer: C. Metamorphic rocks are formed by solid-state changes in pre-existing rocks due to changes in temperature and pressure conditions. In contrast, igneous rocks form through melting, and sedimentary rocks can form through dissolution and other surficial processes.
questions.de: Welche Gesteinsart entsteht, wenn Hitze und Druck ein bereits vorhandenes Gestein umwandeln, während es größtenteils fest bleibt?
questions.en: What type of rock forms when heat and pressure change a pre-existing rock while it stays mostly solid?

timeline.labelEn: James Hutton describes Scottish Highland rocks as former sedimentary rocks transformed by great heat
timeline.labelDe: James Hutton beschreibt Gesteine der schottischen Highlands als einstige Sedimentgesteine, die große Hitze umgewandelt hat

questions.notes: Card correct: metamorphic rock forms when a protolith is subjected to heat (above ~150–200 °C) and often pressure, remaining mostly solid while it recrystallizes (Wikipedia: Metamorphic rock). Timeline: Hutton, 1795 (same page).

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] Which planet is known as the “Red Planet”?
A. Jupiter B. Mars C. Venus
Answer: B. Mars is known as the “Red Planet” due to its reddish appearance, which is caused by iron oxide or rust on its surface.
questions.de: Welcher Planet, dessen Oberfläche durch Eisenoxid gefärbt ist, wird der „Rote Planet“ genannt?
questions.en: Which planet, coloured by iron oxide on its surface, is known as the “Red Planet”?

timeline.labelEn: Mariner 4 makes the first successful flyby of Mars, returning the first close-up images
timeline.labelDe: Mariner 4 fliegt als erste Sonde erfolgreich am Mars vorbei und liefert die ersten Nahaufnahmen

questions.notes: Card correct: Mars is known as the Red Planet for its orange-red appearance, caused by iron(III) oxide and goethite on its surface (Wikipedia: Mars). Mariner 4's closest approach on 15 July 1965 is from the same page.
